summary: SAML claim truncation for users with long Okta profiles causing 403 on role resolution
description: Issue summary: Several internal users (mostly contractors and collaborators with long display names and multiple group memberships) are able to complete the Okta SSO flow (IDP redirects successfully) but receive a 403 when the Redwood RBAC service attempts to resolve roles. The IdP assertion shows expected groups but our auth-proxy is truncating the HTTP header used to forward SAML claims to RBAC, resulting in missing group claims and therefore no roles.
impact: Multiple internal engineering and infra contractors cannot access the Console and developer tools. Affected users report 'Access denied' after successful Okta authentication. Estimated ~12 users impacted so far (oncall requests spike). No customer-facing impact but blocks internal runbooks and deployments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create an Okta test user with a long displayName (>120 chars) and add to 20+ Okta groups with long group names (contractor-<company>-...)
2) Attempt SSO login to console.redwood.internal using Okta SAML SSO
3) Observe IDP redirect completes and SAML assertion accepted by auth-proxy
4) auth-proxy forwards user claims to /api/internal/v1/rbac/resolve but RBAC returns 403 because group claims are missing or truncated
5) Reproduce by capturing auth-proxy -> RBAC request headers and comparing with original SAML assertion payload from IdP
logs: 2026-03-12T09:14:23Z auth-proxy INFO Received SAML assertion for user: jessica.longname.contractor@example.com
2026-03-12T09:14:23Z rbac WARN Missing group claim for user: jessica.longname.contractor@example.com; resolved_roles=[]
2026-03-12T09:14:24Z console ERROR 403 on /console/login callback for session=sess_ox7...
investigation_notes:
Initial triage: auth-proxy is configured to serialize SAML claims into a single HTTP header (X-Okta-Claims) for downstream RBAC. We observed header values being truncated at ~8k bytes by the proxy when payloads exceed the header buffer. Okta assertions for affected users include a long list of groups; serialized header size frequently exceeds 8k. RBAC expects the full group list to compute role bindings; truncated lists cause role resolution to return empty set -> 403.

Hypotheses considered:
- Okta assertion transformation changed to include more groups (unlikely but possible due to new contractor onboarding flow).
- Auth-proxy buffer or proxying layer (nginx sidecar) is dropping/truncating large headers.
- RBAC service has a strict header length validation and rejects incomplete headers.

Quick checks performed:
- Captured raw SAML assertion from IdP: full groups present (verified via SAML debug endpoint).
- Captured auth-proxy outbound header to RBAC: truncated (last groups missing).
- Replayed SAML assertion through auth-proxy with a shortened displayName / fewer groups and request succeeds.

Preliminary root cause: header-size truncation at the auth-proxy/nginx layer when SAML claims exceed ~8k bytes. This surfaced after recent onboarding of contractor cohorts that introduced many group memberships with long names.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:02 - Maya Patel: I can reproduce locally by creating a test user with 25 groups; auth-proxy log shows header length reported but RBAC receives truncated header. Attaching the auth-proxy and nginx confs for review.

2026-03-12 11:15 - Elijah Soto (SRE): Nginx sidecar has client_header_buffer_size 8k and large_client_header_buffers 1 8k in the default config. Increasing buffers may be required. Will try staging patch.

2026-03-12 13:40 - Riley Chen: As an immediate workaround, I created a short-lived mapping rule on auth-proxy to compact group names (strip prefixes) for contractor groups to reduce header size; tested with affected user — access restored. This is sledgehammer but buys time.

2026-03-13 08:03 - Maya Patel: Rolling change to staging nginx sidecar to large_client_header_buffers 4 16k and bumped proxy_buffer_size. Running smoke tests now. Need follow-up for a safer long-term design (move claim payload to POST body or use signed JWT instead of large header).
resolution: Workaround: Auth-proxy temporary name compaction rule applied for contractor groups to reduce header size and restore access for impacted users. Short-term fix deployed to staging: increase nginx header buffers (large_client_header_buffers 4 16k) and proxy_buffer_size increased. Long-term solution options: (1) stop encoding entire SAML assertion into a single header and instead POST signed JWT to RBAC; (2) persist assertion to internal S3-like store and pass a reference token; (3) trim non-essential group name prefixes during IdP transform. Engineering plan: implement JWT handoff in auth-proxy (design doc in progress).
